plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Dense, layered pompons and shaggy spider blooms crowd Japanese gardens and temple grounds in a blaze of warm autumn color. Their spicy, earthy scent drifts through the cool air as other flowers fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn, peaking from October through November in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan and temperate East Asia, including Kyoto and Tokyo
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants. They set buds only when nights grow long enough, which is why they bloom so reliably in autumn. Japan's imperial family uses a 16-petal chrysanthemum as its crest.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in Australia and South Africa turn violet-blue as these trees bloom. Clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers cover the branches and carpet the pavement below in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, typically October to November
plants.location: Pretoria in South Africa, and Brisbane and Sydney in Australia
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of street trees. The tree comes from South America, not Africa or Australia.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Delicate, daisy-like flowers bob on thin stems above feathery, fern-like leaves. They glow in late-season sun in warm regions, and the blooms keep coming until the first hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through the first frost, often continuing through October in mild climates
plants.location: Mexico, its native range, and warm-autumn gardens across the Americas
plants.funFact: Cosmos takes its name from the Greek word for order or harmony, a nod to the neat symmetry of its petals. The flowers are also edible and attract many pollinators.
